title: Harden the merge driver command: a driver that cannot run loses their changes silently
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-19 while building 70i.8. When the command in `merge.version-manager.driver` cannot RUN at all, git reports `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in package.json` and marks the path UU — but the file left in the working tree is OURS verbatim, with NO conflict markers. An author who sees the conflict, opens the file, finds nothing to resolve and runs `git add package.json && git commit` SILENTLY DISCARDS the other side's package.json changes entirely (probe: their new dependency was simply gone).

This is the exact shape critical rule 6 exists to prevent: a failed measurement arriving as a calm, plausible result. It is a trap the driver INTRODUCES — without any driver, git writes conflict markers and the loss cannot happen.

HOW LIKELY. The registered command is `npx @justinhaaheim/version-manager merge-driver %O %A %B`. npx cannot resolve this GitHub-only package without node_modules, which is the same failure the hooks already carry `nonFatalSuffix` for. A `git worktree add` produces exactly that state and SHARES .git/config, so the driver is registered while node_modules is absent.

PINNED BY a test in tests/integration/merge-driver.test.ts ("a driver command that cannot RUN leaves a conflict with no markers (known trap)"), which uses `false` as the driver command. The README documents it under "Known limitations".
design:
FIX SHAPES CONSIDERED, none implemented — this is a design decision, not a typo.

A. WRAP THE COMMAND WITH A CHANGED-FILE GUARD (most robust found).
   `cp %A $tmp; <driver> %O %A %B; c=$?; if [ $c -ne 0 ] && cmp -s %A $tmp; then git merge-file %A %O %B; exit $?; fi; exit $c`
   Correct because our driver only ever writes %A through git merge-file: non-zero AND %A byte-identical to ours means the driver did nothing, so do the normal merge. Cost: a multi-command shell string with a temp file living in git config, which has failure modes of its own.

B. DISCRIMINATE ON EXIT CODE. Rejected, measured as unsound: npx failing to resolve the package exits 1, which is indistinguishable from "git merge-file found 1 conflict". The likeliest failure is exactly the one this cannot see.

C. REGISTER A DIRECT PATH instead of npx (node ./node_modules/.../dist/index.js). Narrows the window but does not close it — the same missing node_modules breaks it.

D. DOCUMENT ONLY. What 70i.8 shipped: a README "Known limitations" bullet telling the author not to stage a package.json conflict that contains no markers, plus the pinning test.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING HERE: whether the driver should be registered at all for a package installed from GitHub, given 70i.20 (committed dist/ is stale, so `npx` from GitHub would not even have the merge-driver subcommand).
acceptance_criteria: A merge whose driver command cannot run either (a) produces a normal conflict WITH markers, or (b) fails in a way that cannot be mistaken for a resolved file. A test drives the failing-command case and asserts the other side is not lost. The existing trap test is updated or replaced rather than left asserting the old behaviour.

title: No unregister path for the merge driver when versionMode changes
description:
Found while building 70i.8, same shape as 70i.6 (stale hooks) and deliberately not fixed there.

`install` in package-json mode registers the merge driver: it appends `package.json merge=version-manager` to .gitattributes (COMMITTED, so it travels to every clone and every branch) and sets merge.version-manager.driver/.name in .git/config. There is no path that takes either back.

CONSEQUENCES of switching versionMode from package-json to dynamic-file, or of dropping version-manager entirely:
- .gitattributes keeps pointing package.json at the driver, on every branch, forever.
- The git config entries stay, so deliberate version bumps in dynamic-file mode are now silently resolved to OURS on merge — the thing 70i.8 deliberately declined to install for that mode.
- A clone that never runs install just falls back to the built-in merge (measured, benign), so the committed attribute alone is harmless. The harm needs the config half.

NOT URGENT: nobody is in this state yet. Filed so it is visible rather than discovered.
design: FIX SHAPE: an unregister step that runs when install detects a versionMode that does not want the driver — remove the `[merge "version-manager"]` section with `git config --remove-section` (NOT --unset of one key: a .name with no .driver makes git abort every merge with `fatal: custom merge driver version-manager lacks command line`, measured 2026-09-19), and remove the .gitattributes line we added, leaving any other line in that file untouched. Best done together with 70i.6, which has the identical shape for hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Installing in package-json mode and then in dynamic-file mode leaves no merge.version-manager config section and no package.json merge= line that version-manager added; an unrelated .gitattributes line survives; a test drives both installs in one fixture repo and then proves a diverged merge conflicts normally (exit 1, markers present) rather than aborting.

title: Merge driver registration must be behind a knob, default off
description:
BUILT 2026-09-19 in commit 6db1038 on pr-4-package-json-mode. The merge driver from 70i.8 is merged and off by default; turning it on is an explicit, documented opt-in.

WHY THE KNOB EXISTS (unchanged, and the reason the default must stay off). The driver code is correct; INSTALLING it is what exposes a repository to the hazard measured in 70i.22. When the registered driver COMMAND cannot run, git reports 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in package.json', marks the path UU, and leaves the file as OURS VERBATIM WITH NO CONFLICT MARKERS. An author who sees a conflict, opens the file, finds nothing to resolve and runs 'git add package.json' SILENTLY DISCARDS the other side. Without any driver registered git writes markers and this cannot happen. The registered command is 'npx @justinhaaheim/version-manager ...', and 'git worktree add' produces exactly the state where that cannot resolve while sharing .git/config. Justin uses worktrees constantly. Justin's feature-knobs rule — merge the code early, off by default, behind a knob — is precisely for this.

WHAT LANDED
- src/types.ts: MergeDriverConfigSchema ({enabled: boolean, default false}, itself .default({enabled: false})), declared in VersionManagerConfigSchema, plus the MergeDriverConfig type. Same shape and defaulting style as branchSuffix.
- src/version-generator.ts: isMergeDriverEnabled(), mirroring getVersionMode(). Returns false when there is no config AND when the config could not be parsed — an unreadable config must never be the reason a repo ends up with a driver. Both config literals (getDefaultVersionManagerConfig, migrateLegacyConfig) now carry mergeDriver: {enabled: false}, so a freshly created or migrated version-manager.json writes the knob out explicitly, off.
- src/index.ts: installCommand registers the driver only when versionMode === 'package-json' AND isMergeDriverEnabled(). With the knob off install says nothing about merge drivers; with it on, every message and failure behaviour 70i.8 built is unchanged.
- tests/helpers/repo-fixtures.ts: MergeDriverFixtureConfig, an optional trailing parameter on setupPackageJsonModeRepo and setupRepoForInstall. Omitted, the fixture writes no mergeDriver key at all, which is what every existing project's config looks like.

DOCUMENTED in the README's 'The package.json merge driver' section (commit for 70i.12), which now opens with how to turn the knob on and why it is off.

STILL OUT OF SCOPE, and the knob does not fix either: hardening the driver command (70i.22) and unregistering on mode change (70i.23). The knob makes 70i.22 a considered opt-in rather than an ambush.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean; `TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" npm_config_cache="$TMPDIR/npm-cache" bun run test` with no failure main does not also have (the 8 in the epic notes).

BEHAVIOUR (each needs a test)
1. Default off: install in package-json mode with no mergeDriver field writes NO .gitattributes entry and NO merge.version-manager git config, and its output does not mention merge drivers.
2. Knob on: install in package-json mode with mergeDriver.enabled true registers both, exactly as the 70i.8 tests already assert.
3. Knob on but dynamic-file mode: nothing is registered. Both conditions are required.
4. The 70i.8 merge-behaviour tests still pass, with their fixtures opting the knob on.

title: PROPOSAL: a committed jsonl event log, version derived not stored
description:
SUPERSEDES the timestamp-only proposal that was first in this bead. Justin corrected the premise on 2026-09-19 and his correction is right.

WHAT HE CORRECTED. I argued the commit COUNT was the source of every footgun and had to go. He answered: "the exact count is not as important as you seem to think it is... The only thing that does matter is that it's not broken or badly misleading... Is the number going up? And is it an indicator that two states of the code are different?" He is right, and it changes the target. The requirement is MONOTONIC AND DISCRIMINATING, not accurate. His example: main at 0.36.4 squash-merging a branch at 0.36.500 should just become 0.36.500, and that is fine. The undesirable case he named is the real one: "0.36.4 on main, and the feature branch, and another feature branch, and then someone is testing the app and has no meaningful way to identify what version of the code it is that they're running."

HIS SECOND IDEA, and it is the good one: make the version file a jsonl event log rather than a scalar. "It's easily mergeable because it's jsonl."

WHY THAT IS BETTER THAN BOTH EARLIER IDEAS. Today we store the RESULT (a scalar) and then have to reconcile results, which is why merging needs a policy and a custom driver at all. An append-only log stores the EVIDENCE, and evidence combines associatively: merging two branches unions their events, and the count derived from the union is correct by construction. No policy, no driver, no data-loss trap. His "take the higher" instinct is satisfied automatically and more precisely: a branch with 500 events merged into a main with 4 yields 504, which is higher than both sides, every time, with nothing to configure.

TWO THINGS MEASURED 2026-09-19 IN THROWAWAY REPOS, not reasoned about:

EXPERIMENT 1 — `merge=union` needs NO git config. With only `version.jsonl merge=union` committed in .gitattributes and zero `merge.*` entries in git config, a merge where main appended one line and the feature branch appended two completed with exit 0 and produced all four lines in timestamp order. This matters because union is a BUILT-IN: unlike a custom `driver=` it needs nothing in local git config, so it travels with the repository, works in a fresh clone, works in a worktree, and cannot fail to resolve. The entire 70i.22 data-loss trap exists because a custom driver command can be missing; a built-in cannot be.

EXPERIMENT 2 — per-branch shard files need NO configuration AT ALL. With `.versions/<branch>.jsonl`, no .gitattributes and no git config whatsoever, two feature branches and main each appending to their own file merged cleanly twice in a row, total five events. Different paths never conflict, so this is conflict-free EVERYWHERE — including GitHub's merge button, which ignores gitattributes merge attributes entirely (researched separately, see 70i.8 notes).

THE DESIGN
- `.versions/base.json` (committed): {"base": "0.36.0", "since": "<iso>"} — changed only by a deliberate bump, so it rarely conflicts.
- Event log (committed), one line per commit: {"t": "<iso>", "b": "<branch>"}. Either one `version.jsonl` with `merge=union`, or `.versions/<branch>.jsonl` shards with nothing.
- The pre-commit hook APPENDS one line and stages it. Appending is far simpler than the surgical in-place JSON edit package-json mode needs; src/json-text-edit.ts and the F8 library question both disappear.
- The version is DERIVED, never stored: base, plus the number of events after base.since. Nothing has to be reconciled because no result is written down.
- package.json's version goes back to being an ordinary human-bumped semver the ecosystem understands.

THE ONE REAL TRADE, and it is a genuine trade.
- ONE file + union: easy to consume (read one file, count lines), conflicts only on GitHub's merge button, clean on every local merge.
- SHARDED files: conflict-free everywhere including the GitHub button, but a consumer reads a DIRECTORY, which is awkward for a bundled client app (Metro/webpack cannot glob at runtime). Fine for a Node/bun library, which is the stated target (~/Dev/prompts).
A hybrid where the hook also writes a derived scalar for easy consumption reintroduces a conflicting file, though a stale scalar would self-heal on the next commit.

HONEST COSTS
- The log grows by one line per commit, forever. ~100 bytes per commit; 10k commits is about 1MB of highly compressible text. Pruning at a base bump is possible but creates modify/delete conflicts against branches holding the old file, so probably do not.
- `git commit --amend` appends a second event, so the count runs one high. Justin has explicitly accepted inexactness of this kind; do not build machinery for it.
- Rebase still does not re-run the hook, so the log simply carries through. Stale, never wrong.

WHAT IS KEPT FROM THE 70i PUSH: the pre-commit hook, the index-aware staging from 70i.3, the fail-loudly contract from 70i.4, and optionally the branch suffix from 70i.10, which solves the "two branches both say 0.36.5" identification case he named as the one that actually matters.

WHAT BECOMES MOOT: 70i.22 (the driver trap), 70i.23 (no unregister path), 70i.8 and 70i.24 (the driver and its knob), and F8 (hand-rolled scanner versus jsonc-parser).

STATUS: a proposal. Justin invited it and has engaged with it; he has not chosen it.
close_reason: Built as version-manager-cza (event-log mode): the proposal was adopted with one file plus merge=union (E1), not shards, and merged to main at a6ef373 with cza.1 closed 2026-09-19. The open questions it raised live on cza.3 (GitHub merge-button conflicts, unbounded growth) and on th-si1.9 (whether package-json mode is deprecated). Closed by the 2026-09-26 follow-up push on Justin's instruction.

title: versionCalculationMode is required by the config schema: a config holding only versionMode is rejected and runs as dynamic-file
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-26, during the version-manager-70i.11 dispatch. A version-manager.json containing exactly {"versionMode": "event-log"} fails VersionManagerConfigSchema with `versionCalculationMode: Invalid option: expected one of "add-to-patch"|"append-commits"`. In src/types.ts, versionCalculationMode is the only field with neither .default() nor .optional(). readVersionManagerConfig() then warns and returns config: null, so getVersionMode() returns 'dynamic-file' and the event-log mode the user wrote down is silently ignored. Observed: `watch` in that scratch repo printed the schema warning and then started watching in dynamic-file mode.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW
1. CLAUDE.md says "Every field above is optional in the file; the Zod defaults fill in what is missing". That is false for versionCalculationMode.
2. version-manager-70i.7 M2 and epic design P4 decide that `install --mode <m>` creates a config holding ONLY versionMode, on the premise that every field is optional. Against the current schema that file is invalid. Today it silently reads as dynamic-file; after version-manager-70i.18.2 (F7) it throws in every command.
3. src/version-reader.ts readCalculationMode() already treats a missing versionCalculationMode as DEFAULT_VERSION_CALCULATION_MODE ('append-commits'), so readVersion() and the CLI disagree about the same file.
4. The absent-file default (getDefaultVersionManagerConfig(), 'append-commits') and DEFAULT_VERSION_CALCULATION_MODE ('append-commits') already agree, so option (a) below changes no existing default.

FIX SHAPE (a conductor decision, not taken here)
(a) Give versionCalculationMode `.default(DEFAULT_VERSION_CALCULATION_MODE)` in VersionManagerConfigSchema. This matches the reader, CLAUDE.md and P4, and makes a minimal {"versionMode": ...} config valid.
(b) Keep it required, and instead correct CLAUDE.md, change 70i.7 M2 / P4 to write versionCalculationMode as well, and make readVersion() reject a config that omits it.
Either way, sequence it before version-manager-70i.7, whose M2 depends on the answer.

Found by: version-manager-70i.11 player. Not fixed there, because it is outside that bead's fence.
design:
DECIDED 2026-09-26 (conductor): OPTION (a). VersionManagerConfigSchema gives versionCalculationMode `.default(DEFAULT_VERSION_CALCULATION_MODE)` (append-commits), the constant src/version-reader.ts readCalculationMode() already uses.

WHY (a): it is the only option under which every existing statement is true at once. CLAUDE.md says every field is optional; readVersion() already defaults the field; epic design P4 and version-manager-70i.7 M2 write a config holding only versionMode. The default value equals both getDefaultVersionManagerConfig() and DEFAULT_VERSION_CALCULATION_MODE, so no existing default changes. The one behaviour change is the fix itself: a config that omits the field used to be rejected as a whole and run on the defaults, silently ignoring every other field in it (versionMode, versions, branchSuffix, mergeDriver); now those fields take effect.

REJECTED: (b), keeping the field required. It would force install --mode to write a calculation mode the user never chose, and it would require changing readVersion() to reject a config it accepts today.

BUILT IN THE SAME DISPATCH AS version-manager-70i.18.2 (the config-reading half of 70i.18), because 70i.18.2 makes an invalid config throw in every command: landing 70i.18.2 without this fix would turn every minimal config into a hard failure. Must land before version-manager-70i.7.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A version-manager.json of exactly {"versionMode": "event-log"} either parses with the default calculation mode (option a), or fails with a message naming the missing versionCalculationMode (option b). In neither case does the command silently run as dynamic-file.
2. The CLI and readVersion() agree on the calculation mode for a config that omits versionCalculationMode.
3. CLAUDE.md's "every field is optional" statement is true, or is corrected.
4. A test pins the chosen behaviour, with a recorded negative control.
5. version-manager-70i.7 M2 is consistent with the chosen behaviour.

title: A fresh repository cannot make its first commit, or run install, in package-json or event-log mode
description:
Measured 2026-09-26 by the 70i.18.1 player (decision F4 of version-manager-70i.18), git 2.54.0, zero-commit repository, BEFORE the 70i.18.1 change:

- package-json mode: `install --silent --non-interactive` exits 1. With the pre-commit hook put in place by hand (the exact `--pre-commit --silent` command install writes), the first `git commit` exits 1 and no commit is made.
- event-log mode: the same, both halves (version.jsonl and .gitattributes were created by hand, as install would).

Both fail at the same place: getGitDescribe() runs `git describe --always --tags --dirty`, which fails with "fatal: bad revision 'HEAD'". execCommand()'s "no names found" fallback does not fire (the message differs), and its fallback `git rev-parse --short HEAD` would fail on an unborn branch too. So every mode needs one commit made WITHOUT the hook before version-manager can be installed or its hook can run.

The fix belongs in getGitDescribe() / the dirty measurement, which 70i.18.1 kept out of scope (F4). getCurrentBranch() already returns the real branch name on an unborn branch after 70i.18.1 (F3), so the branch half is done.

Probe script used: a bun script that builds the fresh repo, runs install, then installs the hook by hand and commits (scratchpad probe-f4.ts of the 70i.18.1 session; not committed).
acceptance_criteria:
1. In a zero-commit repository, `install` succeeds in all three modes.
2. The first hooked commit succeeds in package-json mode (the commit records the computed version) and in event-log mode (the commit records one commit event).
3. The dirty flag on an unborn branch is measured, not defaulted: a failure to measure it is still an error naming the git command (critical rule 6, P3).
4. An integration test per mode, each with a negative control.

title: Pre-commit hook must read the INDEX, not the working tree
description:
DONE on branch pr-4-package-json-mode (commits e7987a8, df89647). Awaiting conductor review; NOT closed by the player.

THE BUG (fixed). The pre-commit hook read the WORKING TREE package.json, rewrote its version, then ran `git add package.json` on the whole file. Any unstaged edit sitting in package.json — a half-added dependency, a script being drafted — was silently swept into a commit the author never staged it for. That puts content into history the author did not choose to commit.

WHAT NOW EXISTS (epic design D9)
- The base version is read from the INDEX. When package.json is unstaged the index holds HEAD's content, so one rule covers the staged and the unstaged case with no branching, and an unstaged VERSION edit can no longer steer the calculation.
- The new index content is the index content with only the version value replaced, written with `git hash-object -w --stdin` + `git update-index --cacheinfo`. Nothing else about the index moves. package.json is no longer passed to `git add` — that would undo exactly this.
- The working-tree file gets a string-level replacement of the same value, never a parse-and-re-stringify.
- package.json absent from the index falls back to the working tree, warns, and writes the WORKING TREE ONLY. Interpretation of D9, which specifies only the read fallback: adding a whole unstaged file to the index would be the larger version of the bug being fixed.

CODE
- src/json-text-edit.ts (NEW): findTopLevelStringValueSpan / replaceTopLevelStringValue. A depth-tracking scanner, because "version" is not unique in a package.json (nested in overrides/volta, and a dependency literally named `version` exists on npm). 13 unit tests in tests/unit/json-text-edit.test.ts.
- src/git-utils.ts: readIndexEntry() / writeIndexEntry(). Sync + execFileSync, NOT the module's async execCommand(), because the write needs stdin, the callers are sync, and execCommand() .trim()s its output — which would eat package.json's trailing newline.
- src/script-manager.ts: readPreCommitBaseVersion() / writePreCommitVersion() bodies replaced.
- src/version-generator.ts: consumes the richer read; new GenerateVersionResult.preCommitBaseWarning.
- src/index.ts: preCommitHandler no longer stages package.json; prints the fallback warning.

MEASURED FACTS worth not rediscovering
- `git update-index --cacheinfo` resolves its path from the REPO ROOT while `git ls-files -- <path>` matches relative to CWD. Run from a subdirectory, a bare 'package.json' silently overwrites the ROOT package.json's index entry. That is why the path comes from `git ls-files --full-name`.
- `git commit -a`: git stages tracked modifications into the real index before pre-commit runs, so the hook reads them and the result is correct.
- Partial commits (`git commit -- <path>`): the hook runs against a TEMPORARY index, so the surgical write lands in the commit correctly (the unstaged edit stays out), but the REAL index keeps the pre-commit version and `git status` shows `MM package.json`. MEASURED to be pre-existing: the same probe against the pre-change code (0ef1f60) showed the identical stale real index, plus the unstaged edit in HEAD. Filed separately.

SHAPE DEVIATIONS from the bead text, all deliberate and reported
1. The git-utils helper returns GitIndexEntry|null (content + mode + repo-relative path), not string|null: the mode and path are needed for a correct write and must come from the SAME measurement (critical rule 6.2, "one nullable field, not many"). Null still means strictly "not in the index".
2. readPreCommitBaseVersion() returns {source, version}|null rather than string|null, so D9's "say so in verbose output" can travel to the CLI the way branchSuffixWarning already does.

OUT OF SCOPE AND UNTOUCHED: 70i.4 (fail loudly on a failed stage), 70i.8 (amend/rebase/merge), 70i.5 (drop updateLockfile).
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR. New integration tests carry an explicit per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. THE HEADLINE: with an unstaged edit in package.json (add a devDependency in the working tree, stage nothing but an unrelated source file) a hooked commit records the version bump and does NOT record the devDependency. After the commit, the working tree still has the devDependency and shows the new version, and `git status` still reports package.json as modified.
2. Staged edits to package.json ARE committed, together with the version bump, unchanged in every other respect.
3. Formatting and key order elsewhere in the working-tree package.json survive the hook byte-for-byte apart from the version value. Use a package.json with non-default formatting (4-space indent, or a trailing comment-free but unusual key order) to prove it.
4. The version written to the index and the version written to the working tree are the same string.
5. The existing package-json-mode tests still pass. The self-healing-after---no-verify behaviour is unchanged.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (required, and reported)
For item 1 and item 3: break the implementation (revert to reading the working tree; parse-and-restringify the file), watch each test fail, restore, report the failure messages.
notes:
VERIFICATION, as run.

GATE
- `bun run signal`: clean (tsc, eslint --max-warnings 0, prettier).
- Full `bun test` (recipe: TMPDIR/npm_config_cache redirect): 243 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail, and the 8 are the exact documented baseline set (2 formatVersionOutput compact snapshots, 5 Watch Command, 1 husky bun.lock). +20 passing over the branch's previous 223, which is exactly the 20 tests added (13 unit + 5 new integration + 2 F4).
- Every new integration test carries an explicit 30000ms timeout.

BEHAVIOUR ITEMS, each with a test in tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts
1. AC1 — an unstaged devDependency does NOT reach the commit, the version bump does, the working tree keeps both and `git status` still reports ' M package.json'. This test previously asserted the OPPOSITE (it documented the bug); it was rewritten, not added.
2. AC2 — staged package.json edits ARE committed with the bump, unchanged in every other respect, working tree clean afterwards.
3. AC3 — four-space indent, an interior blank line and `name`-last key order survive byte-for-byte in BOTH the working tree and the commit; only the version value differs.
4. AC4 — the index string and the working-tree string are identical, proven with the two copies deliberately differing elsewhere.
5. The 20 pre-existing package-json-mode tests still pass, self-healing-after---no-verify included.
Plus: an unstaged VERSION edit does not steer the calculation; package.json absent from the index falls back and says so while staying untracked.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all three run and restored
- Restore `git add package.json` in filesToStage -> AC1 fails: `expect(committed.devDependencies?.['left-pad']).toBeUndefined()` receives "^1.3.0".
- Replace the working-tree write with updatePackageVersion() (parse-and-re-stringify) -> AC3 fails with a diff showing four-space indent flattened to two and the blank line gone.
- Revert the read to getPackageVersion() -> the unstaged-VERSION-edit test fails: expected "0.1.1", received "9.9.10".

NOT VERIFIED / KNOWN GAPS
- No test covers the git-utils throw paths (unmerged stage, quoted path, unparseable ls-files line, a non-JSON staged package.json). They are by-construction only.
- No test covers `git commit -a` or partial commits; both were measured by hand in a throwaway fixture (see the description) but not pinned by a test.
- The mode is passed through verbatim from `git ls-files`, so a 100755 package.json keeps its mode. Not tested.
- COST: the pre-commit path now spawns ~6 git processes (ls-files + cat-file twice, hash-object, update-index) where it spawned 1 (`git add`). writePreCommitVersion deliberately re-reads the index rather than caching the earlier read, so it is correct standing alone. Dwarfed by the `npm install` updateLockfile still runs (70i.5 removes that).

LIBRARY-VS-HAND-ROLLED, for the record. jsonc-parser (Microsoft, zero-dep, VS Code's own) has modify()/applyEdits() that do exactly this surgical edit. Not used: it would add the FOURTH runtime dependency to a package whose README makes a point of having three, and D9 specifies a string-level replacement. If Justin would rather take the dependency, json-text-edit.ts is ~150 lines that delete cleanly.
close_reason: Built and verified. Conductor ran the gate twice independently: 243 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail both times, the 8 being exactly main's set; +20 over the previous 223, matching the 20 tests added. bun run signal green. Reviewed line by line. The headline case is fixed and proven: an unstaged devDependency no longer reaches the commit while the version bump does, and the working tree keeps both. The working-tree write is a true string-level replacement, so 4-space indent, an interior blank line and an unusual key order all survive byte-for-byte in both the tree and the commit. All four deviations APPROVED, two of which are improvements on the brief I wrote: the index helper returns a grouped GitIndexEntry so mode and path come from one measurement rather than two, and the path is derived with 'git ls-files --full-name --stage' after the player MEASURED that 'git update-index --cacheinfo' resolves paths from the repo root while ls-files matches from cwd, meaning my literal 'package.json' would have clobbered the root entry when run from a subdirectory. Declining to 'update-index --add' a package.json absent from the index is also right: staging a whole unstaged file is the larger version of the bug being fixed. Negative controls run and reported, including one that shows the reformat eating the indentation. One finding carried to the fix round (no post-condition parse check after the surgical edit) and one architectural question raised for Justin (hand-rolled scanner versus jsonc-parser).

title: stageFiles/updateLockfile must fail loudly, not console.warn
description:
CRITICAL RULE 6 VIOLATION ("failure is not empty"), demonstrated by a test already on this branch: a stub npm that exits 1 — proven to have been invoked, via a marker file — leaves the commit SUCCEEDING with no signal at all. The same shape is in stageFiles(), which catches everything and only console.warn()s.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. If `git add` fails and the failure is swallowed, package.json is rewritten on disk but never staged: the commit records the OLD version while the working tree shows the NEW one. Every later computation counts from the wrong anchor, and the mistake is invisible because nothing is red. This is the reassuring-direction failure the rule is about.

THE CONTRACT (epic design D10)
- A failed stage aborts the commit: non-zero exit from the hook, and a message that NAMES the exact command that failed and its stderr. A blocked commit is strictly better than a commit that records the wrong version, and `--no-verify` already self-heals on the next hooked commit by design.
- No catch block in this path may return a value that is also a legal success value. Where a helper can fail, its return type carries the failure as a distinct member (string | null, a result union) and the caller must handle it.
- console.warn() is not error handling. Anything that is genuinely advisory and genuinely safe to ignore must say so in a comment stating why the commit is still correct if it fails.

IN SCOPE
- stageFiles() in src/script-manager.ts and its caller in the pre-commit path.
- The pre-commit handler's top-level error handling: a thrown error becomes a non-zero exit with a readable message, not a stack trace and not a silent success.
- Any other swallow-and-continue in the pre-commit path found while reading it; list each one you found and what you did about it.

DEPENDENCY: do 70i.5 (drop updateLockfile) FIRST. It deletes the package-manager subprocess, which is one of the two swallowed failures, so this bead then only has to harden staging and the handler's own error path.

OUT OF SCOPE
- The post-* hooks' deliberate --no-fail behaviour in dynamic-file mode. Those exist so a version-generation hiccup never blocks a checkout, and main's nonFatalSuffix was kept for exactly that reason. Do not make them fatal.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR; new integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. When staging the version change fails, the commit does NOT happen: git exits non-zero, HEAD is unmoved, and stderr names the failed command. Induce the failure for real rather than by mocking the whole function — for example make .git/index unwritable for the duration, or put a failing `git` earlier on PATH for the hook's subprocess. If no honest induction can be found, say so plainly in the bead notes and in your report rather than faking one.
2. After that failed commit the repository is not left in a half-updated state that would produce a WRONG version on the next attempt: either the working tree version change is rolled back, or the next hooked commit recomputes correctly from the index. Whichever you choose, state it in the bead and pin it with a test.
3. The success path is unchanged: a normal hooked commit still bumps and still exits 0.
4. Report the list of every swallow-and-continue you found in the pre-commit path and what you did about each.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (required, and reported): restore the console.warn swallow, watch test 1 fail, restore the fix, report the failure message.
notes:
BUILT 2026-09-19 (player dispatch), after 70i.5.

WHAT LANDED
- src/script-manager.ts: writePreCommitVersion() returns void and THROWS, with the specific message that used to go to console.error. Adds an index ROLLBACK: if the working-tree write fails after the index write succeeded, the index is put back, and a rollback that itself fails says so rather than claiming a clean abort.
- src/git-utils.ts: gitSync() pipes stderr and throws `git <args>` failed (exit N): <git stderr>. It used to inherit stderr, so the abort message named the command but not the reason.
- src/index.ts: the caller no longer checks a boolean. New failureExitCode() makes --no-fail inert for --pre-commit runs. New yargs .fail() handler.
- src/git-hooks-manager.ts: the installed pre-commit command no longer carries --no-fail.

THE --no-fail HOLE, found while reading the path and fixed here. installGitHooks() appended noFailFlag to the pre-commit command, and the top-level catch exited 0 whenever --no-fail was in argv. So `install --no-fail` in package-json mode produced a hook that swallowed EVERY failure and let the commit record a stale version. Both halves are fixed and both are pinned by tests.

THE yargs HOLE, same reading. yargs own failure path printed the entire usage screen plus a raw stack trace and called process.exit(1) itself, so the exit-code decision never ran and the abort message was unreadable inside a git hook. A .fail() handler now prints ❌ Failed: <message> for command errors and keeps the help screen for genuine usage errors.

HOW THE FAILURE IS INDUCED (AC1 asked for real, not mocked). A stub `git` that fails one subcommand and execs the real git for everything else. It is delivered via GIT_EXEC_PATH, NOT via PATH: git PREPENDS its exec-path to PATH before running a hook, and on macOS that directory contains its own `git`, so a stub merely first on PATH is shadowed - measured, all thirteen of the hook git calls reached the real binary. With GIT_EXEC_PATH the stub sees every one of them. tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts:stubFailingGit().

AC2, ANSWERED AND PINNED: nothing is left half-updated, by ordering plus rollback. The index write is attempted FIRST, so a failed stage leaves the working tree untouched as well; a failed working-tree write rolls the index back. Both tests then re-run the commit and assert 0.1.1, not 0.1.2 - a skipped version is exactly what a leftover index bump would cause.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all three run and recorded.
1. Swallow restored (try/catch + console.warn around the index write): (fail) a failed index write aborts the commit and names the command -> expect(commit.exitCode).not.toBe(0), Expected: not 0. The commit succeeded with the stale version, which is the bug.
2. Rollback removed: (fail) a failed working-tree write rolls the index back -> expect(indexVersion(repo)).toBe("0.1.0"), Received: "0.1.1". Note the stderr string assertion still passed while lying, so the index assertion is the load-bearing one.
3. --no-fail hole restored (both halves): (fail) --no-fail cannot turn a pre-commit failure into a successful commit -> Expected: not 0; and (fail) install --no-fail writes no --no-fail into the pre-commit hook -> Received: "npx @justinhaaheim/version-manager --pre-commit --silent --no-fail".

EVERY SWALLOW-AND-CONTINUE FOUND IN THE PRE-COMMIT PATH (AC4).
FIXED HERE OR BY 70i.5:
 1. stageFiles() catch -> console.warn. Deleted with its only caller (70i.5).
 2. updateLockfile() catch -> console.warn. Deleted (70i.5).
 3. writePreCommitVersion() returning false. Now throws.
 4. A working-tree write failure leaving the index bumped. Now rolled back.
 5. gitSync() losing gits stderr. Now carried in the message.
 6. --no-fail turning a pre-commit failure into exit 0. Fixed in both the CLI and the installed hook.
 7. yargs default fail: usage dump + stack trace, and it bypassed the exit-code decision. Now handled.
FOUND, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, FILED AS version-manager-70i.18: countCommitsBetween() returning 0 on git failure; findLastCommitWhereFieldChanged() returning null for both "never changed" and "git failed"; getCurrentBranch() returning "HEAD" for both detached HEAD and a failed measurement; readVersionManagerConfig() falling back to the default versionMode on a corrupt config; readPackageJson() reporting a parse failure as a missing version field. All five are shared with the dynamic-file path, so fixing them here would widen this diff across the whole codebase.
FOUND, BENIGN, NO ACTION: isGitRepository() and hasUncommittedChanges() return false on error, but the first always ends in a thrown "Not a git repository" and the second is not on this path.

OUT OF SCOPE AND UNTOUCHED, as the bead requires: the post-* hooks --no-fail and nonFatalSuffix behaviour in dynamic-file mode.
close_reason: Done and verified, and it found two real bugs beyond the brief. writePreCommitVersion() now returns void and throws a specific message; gitSync() throws with the failed command and git's own stderr; the pre-commit path stages nothing implicitly. AC2 is answered by ordering plus a genuine index rollback when the working-tree write fails after the index write, with a rollback that itself fails saying so rather than claiming a clean abort. The two bugs found while reading: install --no-fail produced a pre-commit hook that swallowed everything, so a failed stage would have exited 0 and committed a stale version, fixed in both the installed hook and the CLI; and yargs' default failure path printed a 70-line usage screen with a raw stack trace and called process.exit(1) itself, so the exit-code decision never ran. Verified with four negative controls including a genuinely induced staging failure: a stub git on PATH does NOT work because git prepends its own exec-path before running a hook, so the stub is delivered through GIT_EXEC_PATH instead. That is measurement, not mocking. Deviation approved: stageFiles() was deleted in 70i.5 rather than hardened here, correct because 70i.3 moved the staging onto the index write and left it with zero callers. dynamic-file post-* hooks keep both --no-fail and nonFatalSuffix, verified by reading the installer.

title: Drop updateLockfile from the pre-commit hook (buys nothing)
description:
MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: updateLockfile() in the pre-commit path buys nothing, so it is pure cost — a package-manager subprocess on every single commit.

The probes behind that (2026-09-16):
- bun.lock records the root package NAME but not the root VERSION (grep found zero "version" keys for the root), and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after a version-only bump exits 0.
- package-lock.json DOES record the root version, but `npm ci` after a version-only bump also exits 0.
- So no supported workflow breaks from the drift it was written to close. If closing the drift is ever wanted, `npm version X --no-git-tag-version --offline` updates both files instantly and offline — no need for this code path.

IN SCOPE
- Remove updateLockfile() and its call from the pre-commit path.
- Remove any package-manager detection, imports or helpers that exist ONLY to serve it. Check for other callers before deleting anything: detectPackageManager is also used by the husky/hook-install path, and that use must stay.
- Remove the tests that exist only to pin updateLockfile's behaviour, and keep the one that proves a hooked commit does NOT shell out to a package manager (invert the existing stub-npm marker-file test: the marker must NOT appear).

OUT OF SCOPE
- Any change to how staging failures are reported (70i.4, the very next bead, which lands on the same call site). Do 70i.5 first so 70i.4 has less surface to harden.

WHY THIS IS SAFE TO DELETE RATHER THAN DISABLE: the behaviour is recoverable from git history, no consumer can depend on a lockfile side effect of a version bump (the probes show both package managers accept the drift), and leaving it behind a flag would add a knob nobody would ever turn on.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR; new integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR
1. A hooked commit in package-json mode invokes NO package manager. Proven by the inverted stub-npm test: a stub on PATH that writes a marker file is never triggered, so the marker does not exist after the commit.
2. grep shows no remaining reference to updateLockfile anywhere in src/ or tests/.
3. detectPackageManager (or whatever the husky/hook-install path uses) still works: the existing install tests pass unmodified.
4. A hooked commit still bumps package.json correctly in both calculation modes.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (required, and reported): re-add the call, watch the marker-file test fail, remove it again, report the failure message.
notes:
BUILT 2026-09-19 (player dispatch).

WHAT LANDED
- src/script-manager.ts: deleted the lockfile refresher, the lockfile-aware package-manager detector, and the git-add wrapper. A comment block in their place explains the measured reason and points at this bead.
- src/index.ts: preCommitHandler no longer runs a package manager and no longer stages anything. package.json is already in the index via writePreCommitVersion (70i.3, D9), and the lockfile was the only other thing staged.
- tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts: the stub-npm marker test is INVERTED — the marker must NOT exist after a hooked commit.
- tests/helpers/repo-fixtures.ts: the node_modules/ gitignore comment no longer claims the hook runs a package manager; the entry stays as insurance.

DELETION CHECK (measured, not assumed). detectPackageManagerWithLockfile() had exactly two callers: the refresher and the lockfile-staging block, both deleted. The husky/hook-install path uses a DIFFERENT function, detectPackageManager() in src/git-hooks-manager.ts, which is untouched. The install tests pass unmodified (only the pre-existing bun.lock husky failure, which is in the epic baseline).

DEVIATION, flagged for the conductor. The git-add wrapper (stageFiles) was deleted here rather than hardened in 70i.4, because removing the lockfile staging left it with zero callers. 70i.4 names it in scope; that naming predates 70i.3, which moved the staging of the version change onto the index write (hash-object + update-index). 70i.4 therefore hardens THAT path instead.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, run and recorded. With src/index.ts and src/script-manager.ts restored to HEAD (the refresher back in place) and the new test file, the test fails on exactly the intended assertion:
  expect(fs.existsSync(marker)).toBe(false)  ->  Expected: false, Received: true
  (fail) package-json version mode > package manager side effects > a hooked commit invokes no package manager (70i.5)
Sources restored afterwards; suite green again.

LIMIT OF THE PROOF, stated plainly. The test stubs `npm` only. `bun` cannot be stubbed the same way because the fixtures run the CLI as `bun <path>` resolved through the same PATH, so a stub would break the hook rather than observe it. The bun branch is covered indirectly: node_modules/ must not exist after the commit, and grep shows no package-manager invocation left in src/.
close_reason: Done and verified. updateLockfile(), detectPackageManagerWithLockfile() and the now-callerless stageFiles() are deleted along with the child_process import; grep confirms no updateLockfile reference remains in src/ or tests/. The stub-npm marker test is inverted, so the suite now proves a hooked commit invokes NO package manager. The player corrected one of my key facts by measuring rather than trusting it: the husky/hook-install path uses detectPackageManager() in git-hooks-manager.ts, a different function, which is untouched, and the install tests pass unmodified. Conductor gate run: 253 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail, exactly main's failing set.

title: Remove stale hooks when versionMode changes
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-19 (by the 70i.24/12/21 dispatch, in a scratch repo, switching dynamic-file -> package-json by hand-editing version-manager.json and re-running install). This bead previously had no body; this is evidence, not a spec — the scope is still the conductor's to write.

WHAT THE SECOND INSTALL LEFT BEHIND, all three observed directly:
- All four post-* hooks (post-commit, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite) still in .husky/, still executable. They do not just sit there: the next commit's post-commit hook RAN and printed its version line, so the inferred half of epic item 11 is now observed.
- dynamic-version.local.json still on disk, and from then on never updated (70i.15).
- The lifecycle scripts (prepare, prebuild, predev, prestart) still in package.json, reported as "Existing dynamic-version scripts detected. Preserving customizations." That third leftover is NOT mentioned anywhere else and belongs with this bead: in package-json mode install deliberately adds no lifecycle scripts, but it does not remove the ones the other mode left.

CAUTION FOR THE FIX: installGitHooks() APPENDS to a hook file that already exists, so a post-* hook may contain lines the user wrote. Removing the whole file would take those with it. Remove our line, not the file.

The README now documents all three as a manual clean-up step under "Version Modes: where the computed version ends up" -> "Turning it on", so a user is at least told. That is documentation, not a fix.
THE DANGEROUS LEFTOVER, and a cheap fix shape for it (conductor, 2026-09-26, not built). The post-* hooks left in package-json or event-log mode are now harmless: they run the default command, which writes nothing in those modes. The pre-commit hook left in dynamic-file mode is NOT harmless: it runs `--pre-commit`, and in dynamic-file mode the default command routes that flag to preCommitHandler(), which rewrites package.json's version on every commit. `--pre-commit` has no meaning in dynamic-file mode, because no install there creates a pre-commit hook, so the CLI could treat a `--pre-commit` run in dynamic-file mode as a leftover: write nothing, warn that the hook is left over from a previous mode and how to remove it, and exit 0. That closes the harmful half of this bead without touching any hook file. version-manager-70i.7 (install --mode) makes this switch a one-flag operation and only WARNS about the leftover.

title: Add install --mode so a fresh install can reach any version mode, event-log included
description:
Today nothing in the CLI can put a repository into package-json or event-log mode. install reads versionMode from version-manager.json, and nothing creates or edits that file (createDefaultVersionManagerConfig() has no callers, version-manager-70i.26). So adopting either mode means hand-authoring the config from the README and then running install. Justin's brief, 2026-09-26: "70i.7 (a --mode flag including event-log)".

IN SCOPE
- `install --mode <dynamic-file|package-json|event-log>`: records the mode in version-manager.json, then installs for that mode.
- The mode-switch warning (M3).
- Deleting createDefaultVersionManagerConfig() (M5), which closes version-manager-70i.26 with this bead.
- Tests, README and CLAUDE.md.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Removing the previous mode's leftovers (hooks, scripts, generated file). That is version-manager-70i.6 and version-manager-70i.15; this bead only warns about them.
- install --silent skipping the scripts block (version-manager-70i.14).
- A --mode flag on any command other than install.
- The merge driver (version-manager-70i.22, .23 wait on Justin's answer to th-si1.9), dist/ and tags (wait on th-si1.8).
design:
CONDUCTOR DECISIONS, 2026-09-26 (binding):

M1. THE FLAG. `install --mode <m>`, a yargs option with `choices: ['dynamic-file', 'package-json', 'event-log']` and NO default. Without --mode, install behaves exactly as it does today. install only.

M2. RECORD FIRST, THEN INSTALL. With --mode, install first makes version-manager.json say that mode, then runs exactly as if the file had always said so. The write must happen before installCommand() reads `const versionMode = getVersionMode()` (src/index.ts, around line 493). Cases:
  - No file: create it holding ONLY `versionMode`, as `{\n  "versionMode": "<m>"\n}\n`. Not the full default config (epic design P4): every field is optional, and writing the defaults would freeze today's defaults into the user's repository.
  - Valid file, `versionMode` present as a string: replace just that value with replaceTopLevelStringValue() from src/json-text-edit.ts. Every other byte stays identical.
  - Valid file, `versionMode` absent: add the key. Every other field keeps its value and its order, and no default field is added. A surgical insert is preferred. A round trip of the RAW parsed JSON (JSON.parse the text, set the key, JSON.stringify(raw, null, 2) + "\n") is acceptable. Stringifying the Zod-parsed config is NOT acceptable, because it writes every default.
  - Legacy file (top-level runtimeVersion, LegacyVersionManagerConfigSchema): the result must parse under the CURRENT schema with the requested mode and with runtimeVersion carried to versions.runtime, exactly as the existing migration does. Do not produce a file that neither schema accepts.
  - The file already says that mode: write nothing and say so.
  - The file is present but unparseable or schema-invalid: fail naming the file and the problem, write nothing, install nothing. --mode never "repairs" a broken file by overwriting it. (After version-manager-70i.18.2, reading such a file already throws.)
  - After any write, read the mode back through the normal reader and fail loudly if it does not match (a post-condition, in the spirit of assertVersionReplaced() in src/script-manager.ts).

M3. SWITCHING MODES WARNS, IT DOES NOT CLEAN UP. The previous mode is what getVersionMode() returned before the write (an absent file means dynamic-file). When it differs from the requested mode, install prints a warning naming what it leaves behind, with the manual clean-up the README already documents under "Version Modes: where the computed version ends up" -> "Turning it on":
  - Leaving dynamic-file: the four post-* hooks, the lifecycle scripts (prepare, prebuild, predev, prestart), and dynamic-version.local.json, which from now on goes stale.
  - Leaving package-json or event-log for dynamic-file: the pre-commit hook. This one matters most: in dynamic-file mode the leftover hook still runs `--pre-commit`, and the CLI then rewrites package.json's version on every commit.
  - Between package-json and event-log: both modes install the same pre-commit command, which picks its behaviour from the mode at run time (src/git-hooks-manager.ts), so there is no hook leftover. Say nothing about hooks in that case.
  Name only leftovers that actually exist where that is cheap to check (our line in a hook file, our scripts in package.json, the generated file on disk); otherwise word the warning conditionally.

M4. DOCS. The README's install section and the "Turning it on" parts of both mode sections show `install --mode <m>` as the way in; CLAUDE.md's CLI section lists the option.

M5. version-manager-70i.26 IS DECIDED: delete createDefaultVersionManagerConfig() from src/version-generator.ts. It writes the full default config, which M2 rejects, and it has no callers. grep must find no reference to it afterwards in src/, tests/, README.md or CLAUDE.md. Close 70i.26 when this bead closes.

TEST FIXTURES: install needs at least one commit, because getGitDescribe() throws in a zero-commit repo (known, see version-manager-70i.18 F4). Existing install tests live in tests/integration/generated-file-policy.test.ts, event-log-mode.test.ts and git-hooks.test.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `install --mode event-log` in a repo with one commit and no version-manager.json creates version-manager.json holding exactly {"versionMode": "event-log"}, creates version.jsonl and the .gitattributes union line, installs the pre-commit hook and no post-* hook; a following commit appends one event to version.jsonl. Proven by an integration test.
2. `install --mode package-json` in the same kind of repo creates a config holding only versionMode, installs the pre-commit hook and no post-* hook, and leaves no dynamic-version.local.json. Proven by an integration test.
3. Against an existing, hand-formatted config (for example 4-space indent, {"versionCalculationMode": "add-to-patch", "versions": {"runtime": "1.0.0"}}): `install --mode dynamic-file` adds versionMode, keeps every other field's value and order, and adds no default field. With versionMode already present and different, only that value changes and every other byte is identical. Proven by tests.
4. An unparseable version-manager.json plus --mode: non-zero exit, a message naming the file, the file byte-identical afterwards, no hooks installed. Proven by a test.
5. A legacy config (top-level runtimeVersion) plus --mode: the resulting file parses under the current schema with the requested mode and versions.runtime preserved. Proven by a test.
6. `--mode bogus`: usage error, exit 1, nothing written. Proven by a test.
7. Without --mode, install behaves exactly as before: the existing install tests stay green unchanged.
8. The M3 warning: switching from package-json or event-log to dynamic-file warns about the pre-commit hook; switching from dynamic-file to event-log warns about the post-* hooks, the lifecycle scripts and the generated file; package-json <-> event-log says nothing about hooks; the same mode says it is already set and leaves the file untouched. Proven by tests.
9. createDefaultVersionManagerConfig() is deleted and grep finds no reference to it (70i.26's acceptance criteria met).
10. README and CLAUDE.md document --mode (M4).
11. Every new test has a negative control, recorded in the notes.

GATE: `bun run signal` clean. Full `bun test` with no failure beyond the two accepted baseline failures (the 2026-09-26 baseline in the epic version-manager-70i notes), run outside the sandbox with npm_config_cache pointed into $TMPDIR. New integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

title: Handle amend/rebase/merge in package-json mode (or document as linear-only)
description:
BUILT 2026-09-19. The merge driver exists, is registered by install in package-json mode, is documented in the README, and is covered by 21 tests.

WHAT LANDED
- src/merge-driver.ts — the driver and its registration (6cafc8f).
- A hidden `merge-driver <ancestor> <ours> <theirs>` CLI subcommand in src/index.ts, which git invokes and whose exit code git reads directly.
- installCommand() registers it in package-json mode ONLY, writing `package.json merge=version-manager` to .gitattributes and merge.version-manager.driver/.name to git config.
- README section "The package.json merge driver" (b891125).
- tests/unit/merge-driver.test.ts (9) and tests/integration/merge-driver.test.ts (12).

THE POLICY (D11): OURS — the branch being merged into. Implemented exactly as specified: read the version out of %A, rewrite it into our copies of %O and %B, run `git merge-file %A %O %B`, propagate its exit code. No JSON merger. The -L ours/base/theirs labels are added so conflict hunks are not labelled with gits temp file names.

EVERY FAILURE FALLS BACK to a plain merge-file, i.e. to the behaviour the repo has without the driver: no version in ours, a package.json that does not parse, an unreadable temp file, a replacement that does not verify. Two top-level version keys are caught on the READ side (the value JSON means is the last key, the scanner reads the first) as well as the write side via assertVersionReplaced (finding F7).

MEASURED, NOT INFERRED (all 2026-09-19, with the attribute committed):
- no merge.version-manager.* at all -> git falls back to its built-in merge, normal conflict, exit 1. This is the fresh-clone/collaborator state and it is benign.
- .driver set, .name unset -> works.
- .name set, .driver UNSET -> `fatal: custom merge driver version-manager lacks command line`, exit 128, merge never starts. registerMergeDriver therefore writes .driver FIRST, so a half-done install cannot land there. Pinned by a test.
- A driver command that cannot RUN -> conflict reported, package.json left as ours with NO markers, their changes lost on `git add`. Filed as 70i.22 and documented; this is the one real hazard the driver introduces.
- Rebase keeps the UPSTREAM version (git "ours" during rebase is the branch being rebased onto) and drops a version-only commit as already-upstream.

DEVIATIONS from the bead as written, both deliberate:
1. Registered in package-json mode ONLY, not in both modes. dynamic-file changes the version only on a deliberate bump, and auto-picking a side of a deliberate bump is a bigger footprint than this bead asks for. Pinned by a test.
2. `-L ours -L base -L theirs` added to the merge-file invocation (cosmetic; without labels git names the temp files).
design:
RECOMMENDED: merge driver that takes OURS (the branch being merged into) for the version field only, everything else normal JSON merge. Rationale: main version then counts commits landed ON MAIN, monotonic and stable regardless of how people branched; two 500-commit branches squash-merged do not produce wild jumps. Registered via .gitattributes (package.json merge=version-manager) plus a git config driver entry, both installable by the install command.

CAVEAT not yet verified: a merge driver is LOCAL git config, so it does not run for merges performed on GitHub servers (the merge/squash button). Server-side merges would still conflict and block the button. Needs checking before promising this fixes the PR workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR; new integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test in a real fixture repo)
1. TRUE MERGE, diverged main, driver registered: package.json does NOT conflict, and the merged version is main's version (ours), not the branch's.
2. SQUASH MERGE, diverged main, driver registered: no conflict on the version field; the result follows the ours policy.
3. A genuine conflict elsewhere in package.json (both sides edit the same dependency to different values) STILL conflicts. The driver must not paper over unrelated conflicts.
4. A non-conflicting change on each side (ours adds a script, theirs adds a dependency) merges cleanly and BOTH changes survive.
5. Install registers the driver idempotently: running install twice leaves one .gitattributes entry and one git config entry, and an existing unrelated .gitattributes line survives.
6. With the driver NOT registered, the measured conflict behaviour above is unchanged — the control.

RESEARCH DELIVERABLE (blocking the README text)
A documented answer on whether GitHub's server-side merge buttons run a custom merge driver, with sources and dates, written into the bead notes. The README states the honest answer, including 'not documented' if that is what the evidence supports.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (required, and reported): unregister the driver, watch test 1 fail (the conflict returns), re-register, report the failure message.
notes:
THE GITHUB CAVEAT IS RESOLVED AND WRITTEN UP. title: Event-log versioning: version.jsonl as the source of truth, version derived not stored
description:
A third versionMode, 'event-log', built on Justin's idea (2026-09-19) that the committed version file should be a jsonl event log rather than a scalar. Off by default; nothing changes for anyone until they set the mode.

THE GOAL, in Justin's words: "having a seamless and easy-to-use tool that makes versioning projects simpler, and that doesn't require a human/agent to be constantly needing to remember to bump a version number... can we automatically generate a version number that has similar qualities to the commit hash, but that is easily understandable to everyone and conveys meaningful information about the code being different?" Target shape: a plain library like ~/Dev/prompts. No runtime version, no OTA, no React Native.

THE REQUIREMENT, corrected by Justin: NOT an accurate commit count. "The exact count is not as important as you seem to think it is... The only thing that does matter is that it's not broken or badly misleading... Is the number going up? And is it an indicator that two states of the code are different?" He is explicit that main going 0.36.4 -> 0.36.500 on squash-merging a long branch is FINE. The failure he actually cares about: "0.36.4 on main, and the feature branch, and another feature branch, and then someone is testing the app and has no meaningful way to identify what version of the code it is that they're running."

THE CENTRAL IDEA. package-json mode stores the RESULT (a scalar) and therefore has to RECONCILE results on every merge, which is why it needs a merge policy, a custom merge driver, and a data-loss trap (70i.22) to go with it. An append-only log stores the EVIDENCE instead, and evidence combines associatively: merging two branches unions their events and the derived count is right by construction. Justin's "just take the higher" instinct is satisfied automatically and more precisely, with nothing to configure and no policy to choose.

=== DESIGN DECISIONS, binding ===

E1. ONE FILE, `version.jsonl`, committed, at the repo root. NOT sharded per branch. MEASURED ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not rediscovered: `.versions/<branch>.jsonl` shards merge cleanly with NO .gitattributes and NO git config at all, because different paths never conflict — which also makes them clean on GitHub's merge button, where union is ignored. Rejected for now because one file is far simpler to consume (a bundler cannot glob a directory at runtime) and because these repos are merged locally. The reader's public API must not expose the file layout, so switching to shards later is a change to two functions.

E2. TWO EVENT KINDS IN ONE FILE. `{"e":"commit","t":"<iso>","b":"<branch>"}` and `{"e":"base","v":"0.37.0","t":"<iso>"}`. A deliberate bump appends a base event rather than editing anything, so there is no second file to reconcile and base changes merge by the same rule as everything else.

E3. THE VERSION IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED. version = (the value of the LAST base event by timestamp, or package.json's version when the log has none) with the number of commit events after that base event applied by the existing versionCalculationMode. Nothing writes a computed version anywhere, so nothing can be stale or need reconciling.

E4. MERGE HANDLING IS `version.jsonl merge=union` IN .gitattributes AND NOTHING ELSE. VERIFIED 2026-09-19 in a throwaway repo: with that one committed line and zero `merge.*` git config, main appending one line and a branch appending two merged at exit 0 into all four lines. union is a git BUILT-IN, so unlike a custom `driver=` it needs no local git config, travels with the repository, works in a fresh clone and in a worktree, and CANNOT fail to resolve. The entire 70i.22 trap exists because a custom driver command can be missing.

E5. TRAILING NEWLINE IS LOAD-BEARING. A file not ending in \n makes union splice two JSON objects onto one line. Every write appends exactly one line ending in \n, and a test proves a merge of two branches yields parseable jsonl.

E6. ADOPTION IS ZERO-FRICTION. An empty or absent log is not an error: the version is simply package.json's version with zero commits applied. Setting the mode and committing is the whole setup.

E7. AMEND IS ACCEPTED AS INEXACT. `git commit --amend` appends a second commit event, so the count runs one high. Justin has explicitly accepted this class of inexactness; do NOT build machinery to dedupe it. Document it.

E8. REBASE CARRIES THROUGH. The hook does not run during rebase, so the log is unchanged and the count is stale but never wrong. Document it.

E9. THE WRITE REUSES 70i.3's INDEX MACHINERY. The event must land inside the commit, so the hook appends the line to the index copy of version.jsonl and to the working-tree copy, using readIndexEntry/writeIndexEntry. Appending is much simpler than package-json mode's surgical in-place JSON edit, and src/json-text-edit.ts is not needed here at all.

E10. FAIL LOUDLY, per 70i.4's contract, which stands. A failed append or a failed stage aborts the commit naming the failed command.

E11. package.json's `version` STAYS AN ORDINARY HUMAN-BUMPED SEMVER. This mode never writes it. That is what removes the whole semver-compatibility layer package-json mode needed: prerelease ownership, npm stripping +N metadata, branch-name sanitisation into legal identifiers.

E12. THE BRANCH SUFFIX FROM 70i.10 STILL APPLIES, and it is what answers the failure Justin actually named: two branches at the same count are distinguishable as 0.36.5-feat-a.1 and 0.36.5-feat-b.1. Reuse the existing module; do not rebuild it.

=== WHAT THIS MAKES MOOT IF IT WINS ===
70i.22 (harden the driver command), 70i.23 (no unregister path), 70i.8 and 70i.24 (the driver and its knob), and finding F8 (hand-rolled scanner versus jsonc-parser). None of them are deleted yet — package-json mode stays until Justin chooses.

STATUS 2026-09-19: event-log mode is BUILT, verified and merged to main, off by default (versionMode must be set to 'event-log'; the default stays 'dynamic-file'). Suite went 296 -> 341 passing with the same 8 pre-existing failures.

E5 WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. I wrote that a missing trailing newline makes git's union driver splice two JSON objects onto one line. Measured: it does not — union normalises a newline-less side, and two newline-less sides merged to three clean lines. The splice comes from the WRITE, appending to a file whose last line lacks a newline. Both defences are implemented and tested; only the cause was misattributed.

THE OPEN QUESTION FOR JUSTIN is cza.3, and it is the one thing that would make me hesitate to adopt this mode: version.jsonl is a permanent merge-conflict hotspot on GitHub, because the web merge button ignores the union attribute (it ignores gitattributes merge attributes entirely). Every pull request whose base has moved will conflict on that file. Local merges are clean. The ONLY layout that is clean on the button as well is the per-branch shard layout rejected in E1, which was measured to need no configuration at all. If Justin merges via the GitHub button, E1 should be revisited before adopting this mode; if he merges locally, it is a non-issue.

DEVIATION 3, APPROVED: n in the branch suffix counts THIS BRANCH's commit events, not the total. That is what E12's purpose requires.

title: Build event-log mode end to end
description:
BUILT. Event-log mode exists end to end on branch pr-4-package-json-mode, in four commits: a986a27 (the code), 1c7db38 (the tests), fce9994 (the docs), ba79f47 (one more test). Not closed: the conductor reviews.

WHAT EXISTS

- src/event-log.ts — the schemas for the two event kinds, parseEventLog (a bad line is skipped and REPORTED with its line number and reason, never swallowed), deriveVersion (E3), countCommitEventsOnBranch (E12), the two line formatters, the file read. Pure apart from that read. No git.
- src/version-reader.ts — readVersion(cwd?), the public consumer API. No git, no generated file. Exported as "./version-reader" in package.json.
- src/event-log-mode.ts — the writes: appendCommitEvent (working tree AND index), appendBaseEvent, ensureVersionLogExists, ensureUnionMergeAttribute.
- src/gitattributes.ts — a generic idempotent .gitattributes line writer. merge-driver.ts keeps its own copy for now; folding them is version-manager-cza.2.
- src/version-math.ts — calculateCodeVersion MOVED here from version-generator.ts, which re-exports it. See DEVIATIONS.
- version-generator.ts gains generateEventLogVersionData() and bumpEventLogVersion(); index.ts routes the default command, --pre-commit, install and bump by mode; git-utils.ts gains addIndexEntry() and repoRelativePath(); generated-file-policy.ts and git-hooks-manager.ts each gain event-log to an existing condition.

VERIFIED

- `bun run signal` clean. Full suite 340 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail, and the 8 are EXACTLY the pre-existing set (2 compact-mode snapshots, 5 Watch Command, 1 bun.lock detection). 296 -> 340 is the 44 new tests, 45 after ba79f47.
- THE HEADLINE, in real git: main 2 commits, branch 5, main 1, `git merge --no-ff` exits 0, no unmerged paths, 8 commit events survive, derived version 0.1.8, and `git config --get merge.version-manager.driver` is empty. Squash merge likewise clean; it lands at 9 because the squash commit is itself a hooked commit.
- Four negative controls run and reverted; the exact failures are in NOTES.

DEVIATIONS from the bead as written — all four also in the final report:
1. calculateCodeVersion MOVED to src/version-math.ts (re-exported, no importer changed). Without it src/event-log.ts would import the module that imports it, and the git-free public reader would drag child_process into a consumer bundle.
2. deriveVersion returns a fifth field, countedCommits, beyond the four specified. The branch suffix needs the per-branch count of the SAME set; re-deriving "since the base" a second time would risk a second, subtly different answer.
3. Item 7 said n is "the count of commit events since the base". Implemented as the count of THIS BRANCH's commit events since the base, using each event's "b" field — the bead also calls n "a real per-branch number", and the plain total is not per-branch. E12's stated purpose (0.36.5-feat-a.1 vs 0.36.5-feat-b.1) needs the per-branch reading.
4. src/gitattributes.ts and the two git-utils functions are files/functions the bead did not name. The alternative was a third private copy of .gitattributes handling, and a `git add` with sweep-in semantics inside the hook.

NOT BUILT, deliberately: the watcher and the metro plugin still derive by the wrong algorithm in this mode — out of scope here, and folded into version-manager-70i.11, whose title and body now cover it.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" npm_config_cache="$TMPDIR/npm-cache" bun run test` with no failure main does not also have — the 8 in the epic notes of version-manager-70i. Use `bun run test`, not bare `bun test`.

THE HEADLINE, and if only one test existed it would be this one: in a real fixture repo in event-log mode, main commits twice, a branch commits five times, main commits once more, then the branch is merged. The merge completes WITHOUT CONFLICT and the derived version on main afterwards reflects ALL EIGHT commit events. Do the same for a squash merge. This is the property the whole design exists for, so it is measured in real git, not simulated.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. Zero setup: a repo with a version.jsonl that is absent or empty derives package.json's version with a zero count, and does not error.
2. Sequential commits raise the derived version, in both calculation modes.
3. A base event overrides package.json's version, and the count restarts from that event. Two base events: the later timestamp wins.
4. The derived version is reported with the right baseSource, so a caller can tell whether the base came from an event or from package.json.
5. Trailing newline: after a merge of two branches that both appended, every line of version.jsonl parses as JSON. This is the one that catches the union-splicing failure, so write it deliberately.
6. A corrupt line in the log does not crash the read: the version is still derived, and the number of skipped lines is reported rather than swallowed.
7. The public reader works with NO .git present at all. Delete or rename the .git directory in the fixture and read the version.
8. install in event-log mode writes a pre-commit hook, adds the union line to .gitattributes idempotently (run it twice, assert one entry), preserves an unrelated pre-existing .gitattributes line, and writes no post-* hooks, no lifecycle scripts and no generated file.
9. bump in event-log mode appends a base event and does not edit package.json's version.
10. Regression: dynamic-file mode and package-json mode are untouched. Every existing test passes UNMODIFIED. A test you had to change is a signal the change leaked.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (required, and reported): on the headline merge test, on the trailing-newline test, and on item 10. Break it, watch it fail, restore it, report the exact failure message you saw.
notes:
NEGATIVE CONTROLS — each break applied, measured, and reverted (src/ is byte-identical to its commit; verified with `git diff src/` printing nothing).

1. THE HEADLINE MERGE. ensureUnionMergeAttribute() made a no-op, so install writes no .gitattributes entry.
   FAILED: "expect(merge.exitCode).toBe(0) / Expected: 0 / Received: 1" at event-log-mode.test.ts:113.
   Proves the test measures git's union merge, not something incidental.

2. THE TRAILING NEWLINE, half broken. formatCommitEvent stopped ending in "\n"; the append repair left in place.
   FAILED: "expect(text.endsWith('\n')).toBe(true) / Expected: true / Received: false".

3. THE TRAILING NEWLINE, fully broken. The above PLUS appendLine's missing-newline repair removed.
   FAILED with the real harm visible: "not valid JSON (JSON Parse error: Unable to parse JSON string)" on line 1, whose text was three commit objects glued together — {...}{...}{...}.

4. REGRESSION CONTROL (item 10). shouldWriteGeneratedFiles() made to return output.explicit for EVERY mode, simulating a leak into dynamic-file mode.
   FOUR EXISTING tests failed, unmodified: "generated file policy > shouldWriteGeneratedFiles > dynamic-file mode always writes" (Expected: true, Received: false), plus three integration tests in the "dynamic-file mode (regression control)" block.

5. A FIFTH, unplanned, and the most useful one. The first version of the "log that was never staged" test PASSED with the index-add deliberately broken — TestRepo.makeCommit runs `git add .`, which staged the log before the hook saw it, so the test measured the ordinary path. Fixed to stage only the author's file; with the add broken it now fails on `git show HEAD:version.jsonl` returning "". The lesson is the protocol's: a test nobody has watched fail is not a test.

MEASURED, AND IT CORRECTS E5. E5 says a file not ending in "\n" "makes union splice two JSON objects onto one line". Two experiments say git's built-in union does NOT do that: handed a side whose last line has no newline it NORMALISES, emitting the other side's line underneath. Tested both with the real fixture and with a minimal three-line repo, where the merged bytes were "{"n":1}\n{"n":3}\n{"n":2}" — three clean lines from two newline-less sides.
The trailing newline is still load-bearing, for a different mechanism: the splice comes from the WRITE, i.e. appending to a file whose last line has no newline. That is what control 3 demonstrated. Both halves of the defence are in place and tested; only the stated cause in E5 was wrong.

MEASURED, AND IT SHAPED THE CODE. appendCommitEvent writes the WORKING TREE FIRST and the index second, which is the opposite of writePreCommitVersion's order, and it has no rollback. Reasoning: both writes throw and abort the commit, so the only question is what a half-done append leaves behind. This order leaves an EXTRA line in the working tree (an over-count by one, the inexactness E7 already accepts). The other order leaves the index holding an event the working-tree file does not have, and the next `git add version.jsonl` DELETES it. Losing evidence is the one failure this design cannot tolerate, so the order makes it impossible instead of unlikely — and that removes the whole rollback block package-json mode needed.

DESIGN VERDICT, asked for explicitly. It is simpler, and here is the ledger rather than the adjective.
GONE, and not replaced by anything: the merge policy, the git-config half that does not travel, the driver command that can be missing (70i.22's whole hazard), the in-place JSON edit and its post-condition guard, the prerelease-compounding problem, the semver/npm-compatibility layer, and the index rollback.
NEW: five modules, about 860 lines including comments, of which the only subtle part is ordering events by timestamp rather than file position.
NOT SIMPLER: it is a THIRD mode, so the tool's total surface grew; the log grows one line per commit forever (filed as version-manager-cza.3, with the GitHub-merge-button conflict as the part that would actually annoy someone); and the derivation now depends on clocks, so a badly wrong one reorders the log. All three are in the README.

Built and verified. Conductor ran signal (green) and the full gate independently: 341 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail, the 8 being exactly main's set, so 45 net-new passing tests and no regression. The headline property is proven in real git: main twice, a branch five times, main once more, merged at exit 0 with all eight events present and the derived version reflecting all of them, with 'git config --get merge.version-manager.driver' asserted EMPTY so the test proves no driver was involved. deriveVersion throws when there is genuinely nothing to measure rather than substituting 0.0.0, which is critical rule 6 applied correctly.

All four deviations APPROVED. Deviation 3 (n counts THIS BRANCH's commit events rather than the total) is the right reading: E12's whole purpose is telling 0.36.5-feat-a.1 from 0.36.5-feat-b.1, and a per-branch ordinal is also what a human would expect the number after a branch name to mean.

title: version.jsonl grows one line per commit, forever
description:
HONEST CONCERN raised while building event-log mode (version-manager-cza.1), for Justin to rule on rather than for anyone to fix unasked.

MEASURED: a commit event is 57 bytes. So the log costs roughly 57 bytes per hooked commit, growing without bound and never compacting:

  1,000 commits  ~57 KB
  10,000 commits ~570 KB
  100,000 commits ~5.7 MB

THREE CONSEQUENCES, in increasing order of how much they would actually annoy someone:

1. src/version-reader.ts parses the whole file on every read. At 570 KB that is still milliseconds, so this is the least of it.
2. version.jsonl appears in the diff of EVERY commit, so `git log -p`, code review and `git blame` on the repository all carry one line of noise per commit.
3. On GitHub it is a permanent merge-conflict hotspot, because the web merge button ignores the union attribute (measured, 70i.8). Every PR whose base has moved conflicts on this one file.

OPTIONS, none of them taken:
a. Accept it. For a library-sized repo — the target shape Justin named — 57 KB after a thousand commits is nothing, and the noise is one line.
b. Compact on bump: a base event could carry a `priorCommits` count, letting everything before it be dropped. This keeps the derivation associative ONLY if compaction happens on one branch at a time, so it reintroduces exactly the kind of coordination this design removed. Probably a trap.
c. The rejected `.versions/<branch>.jsonl` shard layout (E1) spreads the growth and, unlike union, is clean on the GitHub merge button too — at the cost of a reader that must glob a directory.

The question is (3), not (1) or (2): is a guaranteed conflict on every GitHub-merged PR acceptable, given Justin merges locally?
